rationale: The buyers are individual indie developers and solo builders who already pay $10–$20/mo for VPS — willingness to pay is real but the price point is very low, requiring enormous volume to matter commercially. The core problem (VPS stock shortages and price increases) is a supply-side infrastructure issue: a Claude-based factory cannot build a VPS reseller, negotiate wholesale contracts with hosting providers, or manage physical data-centre capacity — this is a capital-intensive logistics and telecom business, not a software product. Operational autonomy and buildability are both near-zero because the fulfillment layer is entirely physical and contractual.
solution_plan: No viable solution plan exists for this factory. Building a VPS reseller or hosting aggregator requires wholesale contracts with data-centre operators, payment processing for recurring infrastructure billing, NOC-level support, and physical capacity management — none of which can be automated by Claude prompts and a Stripe link. A solo non-technical operator cannot build or sustain this. The opportunity is better suited to an established hosting reseller or a well-funded infrastructure startup.
